title: collector-routing-and-s3-archive-terraform-draft
body:
Context

This is an engineering-first draft about how we route OTEL/Fluent-bit logs + metrics from private deployments (VPC or on-prem) into two main sinks: a short-term, high-cardinality Prometheus-compatible path (remote_write -> Cortex/Thanos or local Prometheus with sidecar), and a long-term compressed archive in S3-compatible storage for compliance and offline debugging. The goal: minimal infra footprint in customer envs, clear operational boundaries, and Terraform modules that can be consumable by partner ops or our install scripts.

Why this doc exists
- Multiple customers want a small footprint observability agent that can: fanout to internal observability backends, buffer to local disk, and eventually upload to long term object storage (S3 or MinIO).
- Past attempts mixed responsibilities in a single module; upgrades were painful. This draft separates responsibilities and proposes module interfaces and an upgrade path.

High-level architecture (opinionated)
- Collector host(s) (daemonset / systemd) running otel-collector configured to: receive OTLP/Fluent logs, apply sampling/filters, and route to two outputs: metrics backend (remote_write or pushgateway) and archive sink (s3-compatible).
- Short-term metrics and traces: remote_write -> Cortex (preferred) or Thanos sidecar + store.
- Logs: primary stream -> Elasticsearch/Opensearch (customer option) with a copy -> S3 archive (gziped, ndjson per hour).
- Archive should be write-only from the collector; lifecycle/retention managed by an admin policy.

Design goals / constraints
- Minimal number of moving parts in the private environment. Collectors + simple sidecars only. No heavy DBs in-customer.
- Configurable buffering behavior (disk mem thresholds) for intermittent connectivity to the archive backend.
- Support S3-compatible endpoints (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW). Provide simple test harness for endpoint verification in Terraform.
- Patterns must be idempotent and friendly to terraform apply -> destroy cycles.

Proposed Terraform module split
1) ri_obs_networking (existing network primitives + IAM / KMS configs if AWS)
   - responsibilities: VPC endpoints, security groups, kms grants, s3 bucket policy stub (if customer wants to provision remote bucket).
   - inputs: env, vpc_id, allowed_cidrs, s3_bucket_name (optional), kms_key_id (optional)
   - outputs: s3_endpoint, collector_subnet_ids

2) ri_obs_collector (main agent module)
   - responsibilities: deploy otel-collector (daemonset or systemd), config templating, sidecar for uploader, systemd unit if bare-metal, service account + RBAC for k8s deployments
   - inputs (recommended): env, deployment_mode (k8s|systemd), collector_image, config_template_s3_path (optional), buffer_disk_mb (default 1024), archive_enabled (bool), s3_endpoint, s3_bucket, s3_access_key_id_secret_ref, s3_secret_key_ref, tls_verify (bool)
   - outputs: collector_config_rendered_path, collector_service_endpoint, uploader_pod_name

3) ri_obs_archive_policy (lifecycle management in S3)
   - responsibilities: lifecycle rules, object lock config if needed, replication policy stub, retention tags
   - inputs: s3_bucket, retention_days, transition_to_glacier_days (optional), versioning_enabled
   - outputs: lifecycle_policy_id

Implementation notes / config patterns
- Collector config should be a GO template. Terraform module renders it, tests it with otelcol --dry-run in CICD. Keep the template small: receivers (otlpreceiver, fluentforward if needed), processors (batch, memory_limiter, probabilistic_sampler for high QPS inputs), exporters (prom_remote_write, otlp, s3file_exporter).
- For logs to S3: write compressed ndjson files per hour. Filename pattern: namespace_host_YYYYMMDDHH.json.gz. This makes retrieval and rehydration predictable.
- Use multipart upload via the uploader sidecar (faster and resumable). Provide an option to toggle multipart for small/dev deployments.
- Buffering: prefer filesystem buffer over memory for large bursts. Default buffer: 1GB across nodes, but configurable. Document edge cases when disk fills (drop policy vs backpressure).

Operational play (upgrade / rollout)
- Goal: zero-downtime config changes and a safe upgrade path for otel-collector versions.
- Canary strategy (k8s): add label observability-canary=true to one node/pod. Route a sampled subset of traffic (1-5%) to canary collector. Monitor: 5xx error rate, S3 upload success ratio, prom_remote_write error rate.
- Systemd (bare-metal) strategy: deploy uploader/collector v2 alongside v1 on different socket, update routing via iptables or local forwarder, slowly shift traffic. Fallback by reverting iptables.
- Rollback: collector config and binary are independent. Keep last-good-rendered-config on disk (/var/lib/ri-collector/last-good-config.yaml) so we can restore quickly. Terraform should not auto-delete this artifact on destroy to aid rollback (documented opt-in).

Compatibility decisions we made
- We prefer remote_write -> Cortex vs pushing full Prometheus in each customer env. Rationale: less disk and index maintenance, easier to federate and apply retention tiers.
- For customers who cannot use remote_write (air-gapped): provide an optional prometheus_local module with periodic tarball uploads to S3 (prometheus snapshots) and a lightweight indexer we ship in private deployment. This path is heavier and should be opt-in.

Security notes
- S3 credentials must live in KMS-backed secrets (customer-managed if Private). The terraform module supports a "secret_ref" pattern so the deployer can pass in secret ARNs rather than plaintext.
- TLS verification default true. For MinIO testing we provide a test mode tls_verify=false for lab installs but require explicit opt-in.

Example Terraform usage (pseudo snippets)
module "obs_collector" {
  source = "git::ssh://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//ri_obs_collector?ref=feat/s3-archive"

  env                 = "prod-us-west-2"
  deployment_mode     = "k8s"
  collector_image     = "ghcr.io/redwood/otel-collector:2024-11-13"
  buffer_disk_mb      = 2048
  archive_enabled     = true
  s3_endpoint         = module.ri_obs_networking.s3_endpoint
  s3_bucket           = "redwood-customer-123-observability"
  s3_access_key_id_secret_ref = "arn:aws:secretsmanager:...:secret:obs/s3-creds" 
}

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we support filebeat as a first-class ingestion option for customers with heavy apache/nginx log footprints, or rely on fluent-bit + fluentd? (Priya to prototype)
- Cost model: quantify expected egress/storage for a 1TB/day customer with 90-day hot retention + 365-day archive. (Finance ask)
- Test harness: add a terraform integration test that spins up a MinIO container and verifies multipart uploads + denied credentials handling. (Noah)

Acceptance criteria for GA module
- Module deploys otel-collector in k8s and systemd modes with CI validation test that posts synthetic logs and verifies they appear in both the short-term backend and S3 archive.
- Module has documented upgrade procedure and canary rollout steps.
- All S3 credentials and TLS options configurable through inputs only; no hard-coded endpoints in templates.
- Terraform plan/apply idempotent across repeated runs and CICD pipelines.

Migration checklist (existing installs)
1) Audit current collector configs and active exporters (inventory script: scripts/collector-inventory.sh)
2) Provision new S3 bucket (or confirm existing) and attach lifecycle policy via ri_obs_archive_policy module
3) Deploy collector module in canary mode (observability-canary label) and route 1% traffic for 48 hours. Watch for errors.
4) Gradually increase traffic to 50% then 100% over 3 days if no regressions.
5) Decommission old collectors, optionally keep last-good-config for 30 days.

Appendix: Lightweight troubleshooting notes
- S3 upload failures: check clock skew on nodes (multipart requires close sync), check TLS / insecure_skip_verify flag.
- Prom remote_write 400s: metric labels with unsupported characters. Use relabeling processor to sanitize.
- Disk buffer full: collector logs will emit backpressure warnings; default behavior is to drop oldest batches. Consider raising buffer_disk_mb or configuring external uploader sidecar to offload faster.

Final notes
This is a working draft. The next step is a small POC with MinIO and a test k8s cluster, plus a Terraform integration test. After the POC we will convert the config template into a set of small template fragments (receivers, processors, exporters) to simplify upgrades.

Patch history
- 2024-11-18: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-12-05: added module split and upgrade play (Mateo)
- 2025-01-09: included onboarding checklist and example terraform snippet (Priya)
